nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: This study builds a NEW normative model. The criterion is satisfied: A data partitioning strategy with internal validation is used. The study employed a ten-fold cross-validation approach on the training cohort, where the model was trained on 90% of participants and tested on the remaining 10% in each fold, repeated ten times to generate predictions for all individuals in the training cohort. This provides nearly unbiased estimates of model generalization capabilities.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Methods, Normative modeling: 'To evaluate the generalization of our model, we employed a ten-fold cross-validation approach on the training cohort. Specifically, we divided the training cohort into ten separate folds. In each fold, we trained BLR models using 90% of the participants as training data, while including age, sex, Euler number, and scanner as covariates, reserving the remaining 10% for assessing generalization performance. This process was repeated ten times so that predictions of AI values were generated for all individuals within the training cohort group. This methodology follows standard practices in machine learning and yields nearly unbiased estimates of the model's true generalization capabilities.'
